 Search The Site North Dakota Minimum Wage Remains Unchanged as 2027 Raises Approach North Dakota Minimum Wage Remains Unchanged as 2027 Raises Approach
 Andi Ahne Andi Ahne Published: November 19, 2026 Photo by Alexander Grey on Unsplash Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 North Dakota's minimum wage is staying put as neighboring states prepare to raise it in 2027. According to KFYR TV, starting January 1st South Dakota's minimum wage will increase for non-tipped employees 45 cents. This will bring it from $11.85 to $12.30. Similarly, Montana will move its minimum wage to $11.20 an hour - a 35-cent increase.
 When we look at North Dakota's history of raising the minimum wage, it's quite surprising; the state's last increase was 17 years ago, in July of 2009. North Dakota's minimum wage currently sits at $7.25/hr.
 While that may be the legal floor, the minimum wage.
 (Also Read: North Dakota Steakhouse With 80-Year History Listed For $600,000) 
 Looking at job openings where one might expect to make minimum wage, we see employers offering positions with an hourly pay rate several dollars higher than the minimum.
 For example, Mandan's McDonald's has an active listing , offering crew members $12.hr. Stockers at North Dakota Walmart stores can earn $16 - $29/hr.
 Why Not Increase The Minimum Wage In North Dakota?
 Many North Dakota lawmakers believe that competition naturally pushes wages higher without the government requiring an increase. They also believe that it should be up to employers to determine what the job is worth and what to offer in order to attract workers.
 Some people believe the minimum wage should keep up with the cost of living, even if many employers already pay more.
